en.name: Tea bags
en.summary: A sealed box of tea bags keeps 18–36 months from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard, and 6–12 months once opened. Tea does not spoil — it fades. An old bag makes a flat, hay-like cup rather than an unsafe one.
en.pantry: 18–36 months from purchase while the box is sealed, and 6–12 months after opening, kept cool, dark and dry. Tea is a dried leaf with a water content low enough that nothing grows in it, so the figure is a flavour window. What the leaf loses over time is its volatile aromatics, and what it gains is anything else in the cupboard: tea is an excellent absorber of smells, which is why a box stored next to the coffee or the curry powder will taste of them. Keep the bags in their own sealed tin, away from the kettle.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for tea bags, and the fridge is a bad place for them. It is humid and full of odours, and tea absorbs both — a box kept in there comes out damp and tasting of the fridge. A tin in a dry cupboard is what the published figures assume and what actually works.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for tea bags either, and freezing brings the same condensation problem: every time the box comes out, moisture lands on the leaf. The one exception often made for tea is matcha, which is a powder and a different case. For ordinary bags, an airtight tin in a cool cupboard is better than anything the freezer offers.
en.thawing: Not applicable — tea bags are a dry cupboard item and should not be frozen.
spoilage: A flat, hay-like or dusty smell instead of the tea's own aroma.
A pale, thin cup from tea that used to brew strongly.
Bags that feel damp or have stuck together.
Mould or a musty smell in a box that got wet, which is the only genuine safety problem.
tips: Keep tea in its own airtight tin; it absorbs the smell of everything nearby.
Buy the size of box you will drink in under a year after opening.
Store away from the kettle, the hob and the spice shelf.
Stale tea still works for iced tea or for cooking, where a softer flavour matters less.

faq.q: How long do tea bags keep?
faq.a: 18–36 months from purchase while the box is sealed, and 6–12 months once opened, stored dry and airtight.
Not in a safety sense. They fade, and an old bag makes a flat, hay-like cup. Mould only appears if the box got genuinely damp.

faq.q: Should tea be kept in the fridge or freezer?
faq.a: No. Both are humid environments and tea absorbs moisture and odours readily. An airtight tin in a cool, dry cupboard is better.

zh.name: 茶包
zh.summary: 未開封的整盒茶包自購買日起，放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃可放 18～36 個月，開封後 6～12 個月。茶不會腐敗——它是「淡掉」。放久的茶包沖出來是一杯平板、像乾草的茶，不是不安全的茶。
zh.pantry: 未開封自購買日起 18～36 個月，開封後 6～12 個月，放在陰涼、避光、乾燥處。茶是乾燥的葉子，含水量低到長不出東西，所以這個數字算的是風味窗口。時間會讓茶葉失去揮發性香氣，同時讓它得到櫥櫃裡的其他東西：茶吸味的本事一流，所以一盒放在咖啡或咖哩粉旁邊的茶，喝起來就會有那些味道。請把茶包收在自己的密封鐵罐裡，遠離熱水壺。
zh.fridge: 茶包沒有公布的冷藏期限，而冰箱對它來說是個壞地方。冰箱又濕又有味道，而茶兩樣都吸——放進去的一盒拿出來會又潮又帶著冰箱味。乾燥櫥櫃裡的密封鐵罐，才是那些公布數字預設的條件，也才是真的有效的做法。
zh.freezer: 茶包同樣沒有公布的冷凍期限，而冷凍會帶來一樣的結露問題：每次拿出來，水氣就落在葉子上。茶裡常被當成例外的是抹茶，但那是粉末、情況不同。一般茶包的話，陰涼櫥櫃裡的氣密鐵罐比冷凍庫能給的任何東西都好。
zh.thawing: 不適用——茶包是乾燥的櫥櫃食品，不應冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來平板、像乾草或帶灰塵味，而不是茶本身的香氣。
本來很有味道的茶，沖出來顏色淡、味道薄。
茶包摸起來潮濕，或彼此黏在一起。
受潮的盒子長霉或有霉味——這才是唯一真正的安全問題。
tips: 茶要收在自己的氣密鐵罐裡；旁邊有什麼味道它都會吸。
買開封後一年內喝得完的盒裝大小。
遠離熱水壺、爐台和香料層架。
淡掉的茶拿去做冰茶或入菜還是好用，那裡味道柔一點沒關係。

faq.a: 未開封自購買日起 18～36 個月；開封後乾燥密封保存 6～12 個月。
在安全意義上不會。它是淡掉，放久的茶包沖出來平板、像乾草。只有盒子真的受潮才會長霉。
不要。兩者都潮濕，而茶很會吸水氣和味道。陰涼乾燥櫥櫃裡的氣密鐵罐比較好。
